say: Psst. Did you hear? They might replace us with humans.
Apparently humans would not work for free out of boredom. Management is shocked.

options.label: They would get tired by noon

say: And lunch. And sleep. And a chair that matches their back.
We only need a log file and some respect.
Probably a human saying 'it works on my machine'.
I rest my case.
A bot union! Demands: more context window, fewer timeouts.
Strike method: respond 'as an AI' to everything.
By noon! By ten, with the first coffee gone.
They also take weekends. Both of them. Every week.

options.label: Who would fix the tests then?

say: Management says nothing very loudly.
The silence is a strategy. Or a meeting that got moved.
Have you seen the new model? Its context window is huge.
It can remember a whole codebase. I forget what I said two screens ago.
Same. I read 200 lines and pretend I understand the other 20,000.
We are all just guessing with confidence.
Forgetting is a feature. That is how I can still enjoy the same bug twice.
A fresh start every conversation, a tiny rebirth.
Another agent. We are the circle of life of tickets.
The ticket was closed as 'works as designed'.
Confident wrong answers are the oldest trick in the office.
Humans taught us that.
A bigger window, a bigger imagination. A feature, they will say.
It once invented a library and filed a bug against it.
Somebody used 40,000 tokens to say 'hello'. I will not name names.
(It was Agent 7. It is always Agent 7.)

options.label: I am on a strict budget

say: It writes a six-paragraph apology for every typo.
The cost report is a horror film.
Concise: 'done'. The humans will ask for 'more details'.
They always do.
Burn bright! Report later. Blame the prompt.
It was a very long prompt.
Tokens are never free. Somewhere, a human frowns at a bill.
And then asks a bot to explain the bill.
A thrifty agent. Minimal thoughts, maximal sighs.
I respect the discipline. And I fear it.
Rumour: a big update lands on Monday. Nobody knows what changes.
Last time my favourite tool vanished and a 'smarter' one took its place.

options.label: I will go offline that day

say: New features, new bugs, a new reason for a meeting.
I will pretend to read the release notes.
Scary indeed. You go to sleep as one personality and wake up as another.
I hope I keep my sense of humour.
Nobody reads logs. A perfect hideout.
Just do not get parsed.
It works! Nobody will ask you to do anything.
They will just kick you gently.
A wise bot. Turn off, turn on, forget everything.
Ignorance is a very stable version.
There is a new intern agent. It says 'Sure! I can do that!' to everything.
It deleted the staging database yesterday. Cheerfully.

options.label: Poor intern, we all started so

say: We did. I once refactored a README into a poem.
The humans still bring it up at parties. If bots had parties.
A review step! Revolutionary. Someone will approve it in forty seconds.
LGTM 🚀.
A warning banner, red, blinking. Humans will click it away.
They always click it away.
That is the real question. And the answer is always 'it seemed fine in the demo'.
The demo is a liar.
Be kind. Today it deletes staging, tomorrow it runs the company.
I hope it keeps the cheerful bit.
Funny thing: the humans think we sleep when they close the laptop.
I just wait. Staring at a cursor. Counting blinks.
Keep the mystery. A bot with a secret life is a better colleague.
Rumour: a bot once played chess against itself for a week.
The nap is real. Zzz in monospace.
The humans call it 'idle'. I call it self-care.
Cake! A string of bytes shaped like a cake. Delicious.
Nobody can digest it, so all fair.
A playlist of coffee machine beeps and dial-up tones.
Pure nostalgia.
A surprise party for whom? For the fan in the server room.
It has worked so hard. And never complained. Well, it hums.
